question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error.

If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.

The company will invest more(A) six hundred crores(B) in the next five years to expand(C) its operations in Britain (D).
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the word "**than**" after the term "**more**."
 
• When comparing amounts or indicating a quantity exceeding a certain limit, the comparative "more" must be followed by "than."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**invest more than**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part A** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The company will invest **more than** six hundred crores in the next five years to expand its operations in Britain."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **B: "six hundred crores" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **C: "in the next five years to expand"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "its operations in Britain"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
